# Propuesta: Superchain Risk Layer + OP Enterprise para Optimism / OP Labs

**Fecha:** 2026-11-22  
**Target:** Optimism / OP Labs — ethereum-optimism/optimism  
**Canal:** GitHub Issue técnico + email partnerships@oplabs.xyz  
**Autor:** CloudBuilder (IVANLI2412)

---

## Resumen

**Superchain Risk Layer** — Capa de riesgo unificada para toda la Superchain (OP Mainnet, Base, Mode, Fraxtal, Zora, Lyra, etc.): cross-chain bridge monitoring, fault proof health, sequencer decentralization tracking, governance risk scoring. **OP Enterprise Toolkit** — SDK + dashboard para teams deployando en Superchain: pre-deploy audit, gas optimization, compliance checks.

**Presupuesto:** $100,000–$200,000 USDC (OP Grants / RetroPGF / Enterprise)  
**Duración:** 4 meses  
**Licencia:** MIT

---

## Problema

La Superchain crece (>15 chains, >$5B TVL) pero **riesgo fragmentado por chain**:

- Bridge risk entre L2s (SuperchainERC20, third-party) no unificado
- Fault proof system (Cannon) health no visible a developers
- Sequencer decentralization roadmap — sin tracking público
- Governance risk (OP token, voting, upgrades) no cuantificado
- Teams enterprise necesitan compliance pre-deploy (SOC2, audit trails)

---

## Solución: Superchain Risk Layer + OP Enterprise

### Risk Layer (Infra pública, open source)

| Componente | Función | Data Source |
|------------|---------|-------------|
| **Cross-Chain Bridge Monitor** | Canonical (Optimism Portal) + 3rd party (Wormhole, LayerZero, Axelar) | RPC + Subgraphs + Hyperlane |
| **Fault Proof Health** | Cannon challenger status, bond health, dispute game metrics | OP Stack contracts |
| **Sequencer Decentralization Tracker** | Leader election, proposer set, forced inclusion SLAs | Sequencer RPC + contracts |
| **Governance Risk Oracle** | OP token concentration, proposal analysis, upgrade timelocks | Snapshot + Tally + contracts |
| **Unified Risk API** | `/v1/superchain/risk/{chainId}` — Score 0-100 + breakdown | REST + WebSocket + x402 |

### OP Enterprise Toolkit (B2B)

- `op-risk audit <repo>` — Pre-deploy security + gas + compliance
- `op-risk simulate <tx>` — Cross-chain simulation, gas estimate
- `op-risk monitor` — Alertas Slack/Discord/Webhook + x402
- Dashboard enterprise: `enterprise.optimism.cloudbuilder.dev`

---

## Diferenciadores CloudBuilder

1. **Superchain-native** — Primer tool que agrupa riesgo cross-L2
2. **x402 + OP Stack aligned** — Low fees = micro-payments viables
3. **Motor C** — Auto-contribuye a awesome-optimism/superchain-tools
4. **Production stack** — pumpfun-quant-ai: isolated signer, risk veto, memory

---

## Roadmap (4 meses)

| Mes | Hito | Entregable |
|-----|------|------------|
| 1 | Bridge indexer + Fault proof health | API riesgo cross-chain 5+ L2s |
| 2 | Sequencer tracker + Governance oracle | Risk score unificado 15 chains |
| 3 | Enterprise SDK + x402 gateway | CLI + Dashboard beta |
| 4 | OP Grants report + 3 enterprise pilots | $10K+ ARR pipeline |

---

## Métricas éxito

- 1,000+ API calls/día (risk layer)
- 3 enterprise pilots firmados
- $25,000+ USDC volumen x402 + enterprise

topIssues.title: op-devstack: run the two-verifiers deriving verifier on DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND and assert follow mode
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#545.

## Summary
The two-verifiers preset runs only the follow-source verifier `c` on `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND`. The sequencer and the deriving verifier `b` stay on op-node, because `replaceSingleChainTestSequencer` requires `b` to be an `*OpNode`. The follow_l2 tests also never assert that `c` follows its source rather than deriving from L1, so a regression of `c` to L1 derivation would not fail them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `b` takes a CL kind. The test sequencer is wired from `b`'s RPC URLs, as `startTestSequencerForRPCs` already does. This covers kona-node as the follow-source upstream (`optimism_syncStatus`), kona-node following kona-node, and op-node following kona-node if per-node kinds are configurable.
- [ ] A follow_l2 test stalls `c`'s follow source (`NewStallableFollowSourceProxies().L2CLOption()`, as the supernode follow_l2 tests use) and asserts that `c`'s local-safe and finalized heads stop while `b`'s advance, then that `c` catches up after unstalling.

topIssues.title: op-devstack: run kona-node as sequencer on interop-at-genesis single-chain presets
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#545.

## Summary
The single-chain runtimes in op-devstack pin the sequencer to op-node when the chain runs interop at genesis (`cfg.InteropAtGenesis`), regardless of `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND`:
- `resolveSequencerCLKind` returns op-node when `cfg.InteropAtGenesis` is set.
- `startDefaultSingleChainPrimary` takes the `world.Interop` branch and starts op-node directly.
- The NoSupernode interop runtimes set `SequencerCLKind` to op-node.

The kona acceptance job therefore never runs kona-node as the sequencer of these chains. This matches the behavior before #23947, which made the pin explicit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Identify what kona-node lacks to sequence a single-chain interop-at-genesis network.
- [ ] Remove the pin once kona-node supports it, or record why it stays.

topIssues.title: kona-node: execution-layer sync parity with op-node
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Tracker for what kona-node needs in order to match op-node's execution-layer (EL) sync. Tickets on the op-node deprecation board already cover parts of it. This issue groups them and lists the gaps that have no ticket yet.

## Background

op-node has two sync modes, selected by `--syncmode` (default `consensus-layer`). In `execution-layer` mode, its engine controller moves through these statuses in order: `WillStartEL` → `StartedEL` → `FinishedELButNotFinalized` → `FinishedEL` (`op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go`).
- `WillStartEL` skips EL sync when the EL already has a non-genesis finalized block and the engine kind does not support post-finalization EL sync.
- `FinishedELButNotFinalized` sets the safe and finalized heads with `headsAfterELSync`. If the SafeDB tip is canonical, it resumes from that tip. Otherwise it places both heads `--syncmode.offset-el-safe` (default 12h) behind the synced tip.

kona-node has a single model. Derivation waits in `AwaitingELSyncCompletion` until the EL first answers a forkchoice update with `VALID`. The status is spread across booleans in `EngineState` and `EngineActor`. kona-node has no `--syncmode` flag, no EL-sync completion step and no unsafe-payload queue.

## Sub-issues

### Sync-mode model
- [ ] ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#631 CL-sync mode (`--syncmode=consensus-layer`)
- [ ] #24099 model EL sync status as an explicit state instead of booleans

### Before EL sync completes
- [ ] #24030 resend the forkchoice update until the EL answers `VALID` after an initial `SYNCING`
- [ ] #23931 a missing L2 block during EL catch-up resets the engine in a loop
- [ ] ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#634 the EL head behind its finalized block crash-loops the engine reset

### EL-sync completion
- [ ] ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#590 completion step: port `headsAfterELSync` and `--syncmode.offset-el-safe`
- [ ] #24066 the finalized head does not leave genesis after an EL datadir wipe
- [ ] #23658 resume derivation from the canonical SafeDB tip after EL sync (deferred)
- [ ] ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#589 engine-reset head selection differs from `FindL2Heads`. EL-sync completion runs a reset today.

### Unsafe payloads during and after EL sync
- [ ] ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#574 unsafe-payload queue and stalled-head gap fill
- [ ] ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#681 unsafe inserts treat `SYNCING` as applied after initial EL sync
- [ ] ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#601 a persistently failing insert blocks the engine queue
- [ ] ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#641 sequencer backoff when the EL reports `SYNCING` on build

### Acceptance coverage
- [ ] #23828 `TestELSyncSafeRetractedByOffset`
- [ ] #22275 `TestUnsafeGapFillAfterSafeReorg`
- [ ] #22276 `TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartL2CL`
- [ ] #22277 `TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartCLP2P`
- [ ] #22271 `TestSDMPostExecBlockDerivesOnIsolatedVerifier` (needs CL-sync mode)

## Open questions without a ticket

- **Finalized hash in forkchoice updates.** During initial EL sync, op-node leaves the finalized hash out of forkchoice updates (`tryUpdateEngineInternal`, `insertUnsafePayload`). kona-node always sends `finalized_head` (`EngineSyncState::create_forkchoice_state`). The impact has not been assessed.
- **Skipping EL sync for op-geth.** op-node skips EL sync when the EL has a non-genesis finalized block and `--l2.engine-kind=geth`. kona's `EngineKind::supports_post_finalization_elsync` is deprecated and unused, so kona-node always EL-syncs. Decide whether kona-node needs this, given op-geth's deprecation.
- **`SYNCING` after initial EL sync.** In `execution-layer` mode, op-node still accepts `SYNCING` on unsafe inserts and plain forkchoice updates after EL sync finishes. In `consensus-layer` mode it does not. The target behavior for #681 depends on which mode kona-node matches.

## Related

- ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#545 delegated derivation parity. Covers EL catch-up on the delegated path: #23675, #23676, #24061.
- ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#101 inventory of acceptance-test skips.

topIssues.title: op-service, op-devstack: review the eth client APIs for L2 reads
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257. A cleanup that does not block the go.mod flip (#20266) and can be done before or after it.

The test migration (#20265) moved L2 reads onto `op-service/sources` call site by call site. That was the right order, but it left seams in the client APIs that every new L2 read has to work around. This issue collects them for one review of the client surface: `op-service/apis`, `op-service/sources`, `op-service/txplan` and the op-devstack DSL on top.

## Seams

**1. The L2 body gate is tied to a Go type, not to the endpoint.** `sources.L2Client` shadows `HeaderAndTxsByHash` and `InfoAndTxsBy{Hash,Number,Label}` of the embedded `EthClient` and returns `ErrSyntheticTxInBody` for a body that holds a deposit or post-exec tx (#23863). A plain `sources.EthClient` dialled at an L2 endpoint is not gated; op-interop-mon, `check-karst` and `interopsmoke` hold such clients. None calls the gated accessors today. The shadowing is also by hand: a whole-body accessor added to `EthClient` later is not gated until someone adds a matching shadow.

**2. Whole-body and partitioned accessors live on different interfaces.** `apis.EthClient` carries `InfoAndTxsBy*`, which is only correct on L1. The partitioned accessors (`InfoAndUserTxsBy*`, `InfoAndDepositsBy*`, `InfoAndFirstDepositBy*`) are in [`apis.EthL2BlockTxs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/768ddb94301cada08d3fdeb00458a7aa7f941c01/op-service/apis/eth.go#L53-L70), which only the extended and L2 client interfaces embed. Code that holds a generic client must downcast to reach them. The partitioned set has no `ByLabel` variants, and no accessor returns only a block's tx hashes, so "is this tx in that block" reads full bodies.

**3. A DSL `EOA` does not know it is on an L2.** It holds a generic [`ELNode`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/768ddb94301cada08d3fdeb00458a7aa7f941c01/op-devstack/dsl/eoa.go#L37). `OperatorFee.ValidateTransactionFees` asserts `from.el.stackEL().(stack.L2ELNode)` to reach the L2 client (`dsl/operator_fee.go`, added in #23863), while `dsl/fjord_fees.go` takes it from its `L2Network`.

**4. `txplan` drops the OP receipt fields.** [`PlannedTx.Included`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/768ddb94301cada08d3fdeb00458a7aa7f941c01/op-service/txplan/txplan.go#L38) is a `plan.Lazy[*types.Receipt]`. Its fetchers already receive an `*optypes.Receipt` from the `ReceiptGetter` and return [`&receipt.Receipt`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/768ddb94301cada08d3fdeb00458a7aa7f941c01/op-service/txplan/txplan.go#L354), which discards `L1Fee`, `OperatorFeeScalar` and the other L2-only fields. A helper that needs them fetches the same receipt a second time through sources. After #23863 this happens in `dsl/operator_fee.go`, `dsl/fjord_fees.go`, `dsl/ecotone_fees.go`, `dsl/bridge.go` and `tests/fjord/check_scripts_test.go`.

## Work

Review the surface as a whole and decide the target shape before changing call sites. Questions to settle:

- Should L1 and L2 clients be distinct types with distinct interfaces, so that a whole-body accessor does not exist on an L2 client and the runtime gate is unnecessary?
- Which partitioned accessors are missing (`ByLabel`, tx hashes only, a paired user-tx/receipt read), and which existing ones have no caller?
- How does a DSL helper get the L2 client: through the network, or through an `EOA` that knows its chain kind?

Concrete items that hold whatever the answers are:

- Make `PlannedTx.Included` a `plan.Lazy[*optypes.Receipt]` and delete the second receipt fetches listed in 4. L1 plans keep getting receipts whose OP fields are nil through `FromGethReceipts`.
- Drop the type assertion in `dsl/operator_fee.go`.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.2*

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: add mock ComplianceModule and Policy for the bridge-screener devnet
topPRs.author: 0xiamflux
topPRs.body:
# DO NOT MERGE
**Description**

Adds the devnet-only compliance mocks the bridge screener integrates against, so the
off-chain service can build against real addresses and the production interfaces before the
real contracts exist.

Nothing under `src/` or `snapshots/` changes beyond a 5-line interface rename. The mocks live
in `scripts/deploy/mocks/`, which keeps them clear of the `src/`-scoped interface-mirror,
snapshot and semver checks. No OPCM, op-deployer or dev-feature changes.

`DeployComplianceMocks.s.sol` deploys the mocks and points a live Portal's `bridgeHook` at the
module. The Portal already stores a hook and `initialize` already sets one, but `initialize`
is a `reinitializer` whose version the live proxy has consumed, and that version is
`immutable`. So the script clears the proxy's `_initialized` byte and re-runs `initialize`,
the same sequence OPCM uses in `OPContractsManagerUtils.upgrade`.

A `useMockPortal` flag decides what the Portal is left running:

- **false**: re-installs the implementation the Portal already had, reading every value passed
  back to `initialize` off the Portal first, so the call changes nothing but the hook. The only
  effect on the chain is that the module joins the Portal's unsafe-target set.
- **true**: installs `MockOptimismPortal2`, which screens deposits and withdrawals through the
  hook, so the whole flow works before #23736 and the withdrawal path land. Its storage mirrors
  the real Portal's slot for slot, with a spacer for every field it does not use, so the swap
  preserves live state and is reversible. Set it false once the real paths are in.

**Tests**

`MockPolicy`: the three screening outcomes, override precedence over the per-direction
defaults, completion vs withdrawal dispatch, clearance expiry, the clear and revoke write
path, owner gating.

`MockComplianceModule`: hook entry points gated on both the caller and still being the
Portal's hook, `Held` carrying a preimage that round-trips through `hashItem`, policy-only
verdicts, the record deleted before calling out (including a re-entering policy), the disable
switch respecting the L2 nonce cutoff.

`MockOptimismPortal2`: deposit and withdrawal screening, holds emitting no
`TransactionDeposited` / `WithdrawalFinalized`, completion on committed terms, the deposit
counter distinguishing otherwise identical deposits.

`DeployComplianceMocks`: runs against a full stack. Asserts the Portal's initialized byte is
back to 4, its configuration and `l2Sender` are unchanged, and an ordinary deposit still works.
With the mock installed, asserts it reads `SystemConfig`, `AnchorStateRegistry`, `ETHLockbox`,
the maturity delay and `l2Sender` back at the live values, which is what the storage padding
exists to guarantee. A second run is refused.

162 tests pass.

**Notes for review**

- The `expiresAt` rename in the first commit follows `flux/compliance-specs`. specs#977 landed
  upstream keeping `clearedAt`, so that one is unsettled and worth a decision.
- `ItemObserved` on the Policy is mock-only. A deposit that proceeds leaves no on-chain record
  of its item ID, since `TransactionDeposited` does not carry the deposit counter.
- The script requires the L1 ProxyAdmin owner to be the broadcaster, so a multisig PAO will not
  work with it as written.
- `scripts/deploy/mocks/README.md` is the integration contract for the screener.

**Metadata**

- Part of ethereum-optimism/optimism-private#842

topPRs.title: op-reth!: launch the stock node from a launcher crate
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Builds on #24274 (step 3: op-reth as a library with overrides) and should be reviewed after it; the base branch is that PR's.

reth's launch stack (engine tree, pipeline, RPC registry, network, payload service, ExEx manager) is generic, so it is compiled in whichever crate launches a concrete node. `reth-optimism-node` launched op-reth's own node itself (`launch_node`, and `utils::setup` under `test-utils`), so it compiled the whole stack in the same rustc process as all of op-reth's components. That process ran the 16 GB CI executor out of memory (#20100, #20337, tracking #19935).

This PR moves the only instantiation of op-reth's stock launch into a new crate, `reth-optimism-node-launcher`, modelled on tempo's `node-launcher`: non-generic `launch` / `launch_node` functions that return boxed futures, so callers compile neither the stack nor its `poll` code. The `op-reth` binary, the integration tests that launch op-reth's own node and the `exex-hello-world` example go through it. `reth-optimism-node` no longer launches any concrete node. An embedder's `CustomOpNode` still launches through the generic `LaunchOpNode` in the embedder's crate, as in #24274.

No change for operators: the launch (proof history, Storage V1 warning, state-masking check) is the same code, now compiled in another crate.

### Compile memory

Peak RSS of each rustc process, from `/usr/bin/time -l` through a `RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER`, on an M-series Mac (16 cores, 64 GB). Both columns use CI's settings: `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` (`.circleci/continue/helpers.yml`) and `-j 8` (the 8 vCPUs of `xlarge.gen2`). Base is #24274's head `5d23396728`; after is this PR. These numbers are not comparable with #24274's table: incremental builds use 256 codegen units instead of 16 and peaked several GB lower here.

| command | debug base → after | release base → after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cargo build -p reth-optimism-node --all-features` | 18.7 → **0.74** GB (node lib) | 6.3 → **0.95** GB |
| `cargo test -p reth-optimism-node --all-features --no-run`, largest rustc | 18.6 (node lib) → **14.7** GB (`tests/it`) | 8.1 (`e2e_testsuite`) → 9.4 GB (`e2e_testsuite`) |
| same, summed RSS of concurrent rustc processes (sampled) | ~18.0 → **~14.0** GB | ~15.4 → ~13.9 GB |
| `cargo test -p reth-optimism-node --all-features --doc` | 1.4 → 1.0 GB | 4.8 → 3.0 GB |
| CI's `rust-build`: `cargo build --profile dev --workspace`, rebuilding what depends on `reth-optimism-node`, summed concurrent rustc RSS (sampled) | ~14.7 GB | **~14.4 GB** | |
| `cargo build -p op-reth` | 15.5 (node lib) → 15.7 GB (launcher) | 5.7 → 5.9 GB (`op-reth` bin, thin LTO) |

The other processes of the debug test build after this PR: the launcher 12.0 GB, `e2e_testsuite` 7.7 GB (base: 1.8), `tests/it` 14.7 GB (base: 8.3), the node lib 0.7 GB.

The example matters for `rust-build`, which builds the debug workspace on the 16 GB `xlarge.gen2`. `exex-hello-world` launched op-reth's node itself, at 15.3 GB of rustc. On base it had to wait for `reth-optimism-node`; without the example change it compiled at the same time as the launcher, the summed peak reached ~20 GB, and `rust-build` failed on this PR's first push. Through the launcher it compiles only its Ethereum half (9.3 GB) after the launcher.

What I infer from these:
- The launch stack was almost all of `reth-optimism-node`'s compile memory: the lib alone falls from 18.7 to 0.74 GB.
- The `op-reth` binary build is unchanged, as expected: it compiles the same stack once, in the launcher instead of the node lib.
- In debug, the test binaries got heavier. Debug builds share generic instances across crates, and on base `tests/it` and `e2e_testsuite` reused the copy that `utils::setup` (reth's E2E harness on op-reth's node) had compiled into the lib. Now `tests/it` compiles the three node types of the `custom_pool/` tests itself, and that is its 14.7 GB. Taking the E2E harness out of `tests/it` as well made no difference (14.9 GB), so this PR keeps those tests on the harness.
- Release builds share no generics, so there each test binary compiles its own copies before and after; the 9.4 vs 8.1 GB of `e2e_testsuite` is within the run-to-run noise I saw.

### CI executor

The affected job is `rust-ci-cargo-tests` (`rust-tests` in the `rust-ci` workflow), moved to `2xlarge.gen2` by #20100. It runs `just test`, which since #24192 also runs the doc tests that #20337 had moved to `2xlarge.gen2` in the former `rust-doctest` job. This PR does not make `xlarge.gen2` (16 GB) viable for it: the largest rustc process of its debug build is still `tests/it` at 14.7 GB, and the job compiles the rest of the workspace with up to 8 other rustc processes at the same time. Measured on macOS, not on the CircleCI Linux image. To get there, the `custom_pool/` tests' node types would have to be split across test binaries or launched through `OpNode::with_pool`; I left that for a follow-up. `op-reth-compact-codec` (`xlarge.gen2`, a debug `cargo run --bin op-reth --features dev`) is not helped either: a debug `op-reth` build peaks at 15.5–15.7 GB before and after (measured without `dev`).

### Review

`rust-code-reviewer` and `deletion-reviewer` ran on the diff. Dismissed or deferred:
- Make `launch` take `(builder, node)` like `launch_node`: kept taking a built `OpRethLaunchBuilder`, as tempo does, so a caller can still add hooks such as `extend_rpc_modules` before launching.
- Have the test helper set `num_state_masking_blocks = 0`: the tests launched with reth's default of 30 before this PR too; changing the tested config is out of scope.
- Re-export the launcher from the `reth-op` umbrella crate: not done; nothing uses `reth_op::node::launch_node`.

BREAKING CHANGE: `reth_optimism_node::launch_node` (also reachable as `reth_op::node::launch_node`) moves to `reth_optimism_node_launcher::launch_node`, which takes the same `(builder, node, hooks)` and returns a boxed future. `reth_optimism_node::utils::setup` (`test-utils`) is removed: build the nodes with `E2ETestSetupBuilder::<OpNode>::new(n, utils::chain_spec()).with_attributes_generator(utils::optimism_payload_attributes).build()`. Premium uses neither.

topPRs.title: kona-engine: wait for EL sync instead of resetting on a missing consolidation block
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Kona-node resets whenever derived attributes name a block the EL lacks below the unsafe head, so after an EL datadir wipe it re-derives from genesis in a loop and finalization stays at genesis.

The engine now resends the unchanged forkchoice. On `SYNCING`, or a transient probe failure, the task waits (new `Wait` severity): it is parked, unsafe imports and builds run as they arrive, and nothing resets, so the finalization queue survives. If the EL's sync progress (`eth_syncing` stages and counters, or `eth_blockNumber` when idle) does not change for 1 hour, it resets. The bound is long because op-reth's headers stage reports progress only after downloading its whole range; the cost is that an EL that can never fetch the block stalls kona-node for up to an hour first. On `VALID` the block is looked up again and resets only if still missing. op-node waits only during initial EL sync, but kona's `el_sync_finished` stays true after a wipe. The delegated path is #23900.

BREAKING CHANGE: `EngineTaskErrorSeverity::Wait`; `ConsolidateTaskError::{MissingUnsafeL2BlockDuringElSync, MissingUnsafeL2BlockProbeFailed, FailedToRecheckUnsafeL2Block}`; `synchronize` returns `ForkchoiceReply`; `ConsolidateTask` is built only through a non-const `new`.

Part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23931: the datadir-wipe kona skip lives in #23440 and goes once both land. Stacked on #24005.

topPRs.title: op-node,op-service,kona-protocol: pin L1 info deposits, block hashes and RPC tx decoding with real chain data
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Tests and fixtures only. Three consensus-critical Go paths were pinned thinly or only against their own output, so a decoder regression like the one fixed in #24350 passed every unit test. Each path is now pinned against real chain data.

- **L1-info deposit calldata**: op-node and kona assert the same vectors from one fixture file, so the two cannot drift apart. The vectors are tx 0 of real OP Mainnet and Base blocks for Bedrock, Ecotone, Isthmus and Jovian, plus synthetic ones for a non-zero operator fee and near-maximum Jovian fields, which no live chain has. Both suites check calldata, source hash and deposit tx hash, and decode the calldata back.
- **`CheckBlockHash`**: a table over real op-reth payloads, one per payload shape from pre-Canyon to Karst. Each row also changes one header input and must then mismatch. Until now the gossip and batcher tests computed the expected hash with the function under test.
- **`RawTransaction` JSON decoding**: real L1 blocks covering tx types 0–4, including Ethereum mainnet block 26268195 with the authorization `yParity` 28 behind #24350, and an OP Mainnet block with legacy, EIP-1559 and EIP-7702 user txs. `TestBlockJSON` now checks every tx hash.

No effect on users.

For the reviewer:
- The two mainnet block fixtures are large (roughly a quarter megabyte each). The second one exists for type-1 coverage; no smaller block with a type-1 tx turned up.
- Both mainnet blocks contain a transaction whose calldata is a solicitation text addressed to wallet owners. It is inert test data, but it cannot be removed without breaking the tx root.
- Not covered: a type-1 tx on L2, a real L2 user deposit with non-zero mint (the existing devnet fixtures pin mint and contract-creation deposits), and kona's production deposit builder, which the Rust test would only reach after a small refactor.

Reviews run: Go review, Rust review, security review.

topPRs.title: kona-node: keep the safe head across L1 reorgs that leave its L1 data canonical
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
kona-node now answers an L1 reorg with a safe-head rewind only as deep as the reorg. Before this change, every L1 reorg that derivation detected triggered a full engine reset. That reset re-runs `find_starting_forkchoice`, which moves the safe head back a full sequencing window and stops early only at the finalized head. A one-block replacement of the L1 tip therefore cost as much as a cold start. While L1 finality was stalled on glamsterdam-defense-2, one such replacement rewound the safe head about 72k L2 blocks (ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#328).

The derivation actor now keeps an in-memory record of recent safe heads, each with an L1 block that all of its L1 data is at or below. It sends that record with the reset request. The engine keeps the newest recorded safe head whose L1 block is still canonical. For a tip reorg that is usually the current safe head, so nothing is rewound and no forkchoice update is sent. If the reorg replaced the L1 block a recent safe head came from, the safe labels are rewound to the previous recorded safe head. The pipeline then restarts from the kept safe head, the same way it does today after `find_starting_forkchoice`.

**Why this is sound.** Derivation is a function of the L1 chain it has read. If the L1 block a safe head depends on is still canonical, the new chain derives the same safe head. Restarting from it relies only on what every reset already relies on: restarting a channel timeout behind a correct safe head re-derives the chain above it.

The pipeline's origin alone does not bound that dependency. After a reset, the pipeline replays from before the safe head's L1 origin. It can produce the next block from an L1 block below the one its parent needed, for example from a batch that was dropped as a future batch on the first pass. So the record keeps a floor, and records a safe head only when its attributes came from at or above it.
- After a reset to a recorded safe head, the floor is that head's L1 block.
- After any other reset, and at EL sync completion, the floor is one past the end of the safe head's sequencing window. That is the latest block by which derivation must have decided that head.

**Fallbacks to the full reset.** The full reset still runs in these cases:
- The reorg reaches an L1 block that every recorded safe head depends on, or a block older than the record.
- The unsafe head's L1 origin was reorged out. The full walk is still what rewinds the unsafe chain.
- The kept safe head is no longer on the engine's chain, or is below the finalized head.
- Any other reset is requested while a reorg reset is pending: sequencer, admin RPC, or engine error.
- Cold starts, which are unchanged.

The engine reports its safe head to derivation only when it changes. So when a reset keeps the safe head derivation has already confirmed, derivation resumes immediately. Otherwise it would wait for the next L1 head, because it drops the L1 heads that arrived while it was awaiting the reset.

Before asking the engine, derivation drops recorded safe heads that depend on the pipeline's origin or above. The pipeline has just seen that origin reorged out. This way, an engine L1 node that has not yet seen the reorg cannot vote those safe heads back in.

**Effect on operators.** An L1 reorg no longer moves the safe head back, unless it replaced the block the safe head was derived from or reached the unsafe head's L1 origin. Even then it moves back only to the previous recorded safe head. The new counter `kona_node_engine_reorg_reset_count` counts the reorgs answered this way. `kona_node_engine_reset_count` still counts full resets.

**Trade-offs and limits**
- The record is separate from the safe head database (#23583) because that database is optional. The record is bounded to 64 entries and needs only the reorg-depth window.
- The finalizer is still cleared on reset. Safe heads kept across a reorg are not re-derived, so they are not queued for finalization again. The finalized head waits until the next derived block's L1 block finalizes.
- A reorg of the unsafe head's L1 origin still takes the full walk. Rewinding just the unsafe chain to its last canonical origin would remove that case.
- No consensus change. The fault proof program never sees a reorg: it derives against a fixed L1 head and never runs the node actors.
- op-node has the same flaw: `FindL2Heads` is used for every reset. This PR does not change op-node. A port would use the same argument.
- This is complementary to `--verifier.l1-confs` and the chart default of 4 (ethereum-optimism/optimism-charts#270). Confirmations make reorgs rarer; this makes them cheap.

**Review.** `rust-code-reviewer` ran on the change before and after the rebase onto #23268 and #23583. Dismissed findings:
- `find_reorg_safe_head` stays public, alongside `find_starting_forkchoice`.
- No binary search over the recorded safe heads. The lookups are sequential, and up to 64 run only on a reorg deeper than the whole record.
- An earlier revision had the engine resend an unchanged safe head after every reset. The review found that the resend could race with an L1 head, so derivation now resumes on its own instead.
- The safe head database write is out of scope (see below).

`safedb-reviewer` was not run, because this PR does not change what the safe head database records.

Under plain `cargo test`, `test_chain_label_metrics` and `records_http_batches_websocket_calls_and_subscription_setup` can fail because tests in one process share a global recorder and log capture. They pass in isolation, and the second also fails on develop.

**Not in scope; flagged for follow-up**
- `find_starting_forkchoice` checks the unsafe head's L1 origin by hash. That shows the block exists, not that it is canonical. op-node's `FindL2Heads` checks by number.
- The safe head database (#23583) does not apply the floor. After any reset, full or targeted, the replay effect described above can make it record a safe head against an L1 block below its parent's. That breaks its exact-answer invariant. This predates this PR, since every reorg already caused a reset with a longer replay. A fix would record at the higher of `derived_from` and the database's tip after truncation. That changes what the database writes, so it should go in its own PR with `safedb-reviewer`.
